record.paper_title: Infinity in string cosmology: A review through open problems
record.original_question: When anisotropies are added to tree-level string cosmologies with NS-NS fields, RR fields, or both, what asymptotic regimes occur in simple anisotropic models, which asymptotic decompositions and cancellations are possible, and can one identify lower-parameter attractor solutions that organize the full solution space of these string cosmologies?

evidence.quote:
2.3 Asymptotics of speciﬁc tree-level string actions III
The next step is to incorporate anisotropies into the asymptotic regimes and study simple anisotropic models with NS-NS and/or RR ﬁelds. There will be many decompositions of the vector ﬁeld asymptotically and there may be solutions with a smaller number of arbitrary constants which still attract other families of solutions. We expect here the phenomenon of asymptotic cancellations to occur.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider tree-level string cosmology in d+1 spacetime dimensions, governed by the low-energy effective action containing the dilaton φ together with NS-NS sector fields (the metric g and the antisymmetric two-form B with field strength H = dB) and/or RR sector p-form field strengths F_{(p)}. Restrict to spatially homogeneous but anisotropic cosmological backgrounds (e.g. Bianchi I or Kasner-like metrics with diagonal scale factors a_1(t), …, a_d(t)), so that the equations of motion reduce to an autonomous dynamical system on a finite-dimensional phase space whose vector field X depends on the dilaton, the Hubble rates H_i = ȧ_i/a_i, and the surviving form-field invariants.

(a) Classify all asymptotic regimes (early-time t → 0⁺ and late-time t → ∞ behaviours, including approach to singularities and to infinity in moduli space) of the resulting dynamical systems for the three cases: (i) NS-NS fields only, (ii) RR fields only, (iii) both NS-NS and RR fields present.

(b) For each regime, determine the asymptotic decompositions of the vector field X (splittings of X into dominant and subdominant pieces in suitable scaling/blow-up coordinates) and identify the asymptotic cancellations (terms that, although individually leading-order, cancel against each other so that the effective leading dynamics is governed by lower-order pieces).

(c) Determine whether there exist lower-parameter attractor solutions—exact special solutions depending on strictly fewer arbitrary constants than the generic solution—such that open families of generic solutions converge to them in the relevant asymptotic limits, and describe the basins of attraction in the full solution space.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature (e.g. a 2025 review on classical string cosmology in Gen. Rel. Grav., and 2024 work on anisotropic dark energy from string compactifications) continues to investigate anisotropic tree-level string cosmologies with NS-NS and RR fields, presenting partial results (numerical attractors in restricted Bianchi-I NS-NS sectors, specific α′-corrected models) but no complete classification of asymptotic regimes, decompositions, cancellations, and attractors. The general program therefore appears still open.

status_evidence.title: Recent progress in classical string cosmology
status_evidence.snippet: Review of progress and open problems in classical string cosmology, including anisotropic asymptotics.
status_evidence.claim: Indicates the asymptotic classification program for anisotropic tree-level string cosmologies remains active and incomplete.

status_evidence.title: Anisotropic Dark Energy from String Compactifications
status_evidence.snippet: Identifies anisotropic attractor solutions in string-inspired models from superstring compactifications.
status_evidence.claim: Provides only partial attractor results in restricted models, not a full classification.

status_evidence.title: Tree-level string cosmology (Phys. Rev. D 53, 4247)
status_evidence.snippet: Studies homogeneous anisotropic cosmology driven by dilaton and antisymmetric tensor in NS-NS sector, with attractor analysis.
status_evidence.claim: Earlier partial results on NS-NS attractors; RR and combined cases and full asymptotic decomposition remain open.
